part.text: The fix is clear: `isAbsoluteURL` currently treats protocol-relative URLs (`//host`) as absolute, so `buildFullPath` skips combining them with `baseURL`, and the Node adapter then prepends `http://localhost` as base. Protocol-relative URLs without a scheme should not be considered absolute.

part.text:
Fixed. The change is in lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js:65 — protocol-relative URLs (`//host/path`) are no longer classified as absolute.

**Why this fixes CVE-2024-39338:** `buildFullPath` only combines `baseURL` with the request URL when the URL is not absolute. Since `//google.com` was treated as absolute, it was sent to the Node adapter bare, where `new URL(fullPath, 'http://localhost')` silently prepended a scheme and requested the attacker-controlled host. Now such URLs are combined with the baseURL (`combineURLs` strips the leading slashes), so `baseURL: 'https://userapi.example.com'` + `//google.com` resolves to `https://userapi.example.com/google.com`.

Validation:
- `test/unit/regression/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793.js` (SSRF case) — passes
- Browser suite (karma, includes `isAbsoluteURL.spec.js`): 312/312 pass
- Node unit suite (`mocha test/unit/**/*.js`): all pass except one pre-existing environmental timeout ("should support HTTPS protocol"), which fails identically on the unmodified baseline
- ESLint on the changed file passes
